obligations.text: Every exp and ln reachable from a pure command is computed by rustev_core::math, one pure Rust implementation (libm =0.2.16, default features off) on every target; no pure crate calls f64::exp, f64::ln or another platform math function, and a test fails when one does.
Changing the implementation's pin is a reviewed change that runs spec 027's differential corpus and every golden on every target; it never happens through an unpinned update.

sectionHeadings: 047: One implementation of exp and ln on every target (amends 002 and 027)
record.summary: Approved (A-44). The remedy spec 027 3.11.5 names for a cross-target floating-point divergence. The pure crates' four transcendental call sites (`exp` in core's softmax, `ln` in core's calibration, `ln` in evaluation's log loss and temperature fit) call the platform's math library on native targets and Rust's bundled one on WebAssembly; measured on 2026-10-21 they differ by one unit in the last place on 0.08% to 7.1% of a million inputs per input domain (macOS arm64 against `wasm32-unknown-unknown`). This spec routes all four through one pure Rust implementation, the `libm` crate exact-pinned at 0.2.16 without default features, exposed as `rustev_core::math`, so each produces the same bits on every target; no existing golden changes. Ratified by the owner on 2026-10-21 (A-44). Approval does not authorize a release.
